_meta.name: India outpatient formulary
_meta.source_note: Adult dose limits, renal/hepatic adjustments and cautions compiled from standard prescribing references (National Formulary of India, BNF, AGS Beers Criteria 2023 and product labelling). Decision support only: verify against current local prescribing information.

interactions.title: Major bleeding risk
interactions.note: Anticoagulant with an NSAID or aspirin markedly increases GI and other bleeding. Avoid; if unavoidable, add PPI cover and review.

interactions.title: Bleeding risk
interactions.note: Anticoagulant plus antiplatelet — confirm the indication and planned duration.

interactions.title: Two anticoagulants
interactions.note: Two anticoagulants together — only during a planned switch.

interactions.title: GI bleeding risk
interactions.note: NSAID with antiplatelet therapy increases GI bleeding; ibuprofen may blunt aspirin's antiplatelet effect. Consider paracetamol and PPI cover.

interactions.title: INR will rise
interactions.note: Inhibits warfarin metabolism — INR can rise sharply. Avoid or reduce warfarin and check INR within 3–5 days.

interactions.title: Reduced clopidogrel effect
interactions.note: Omeprazole/esomeprazole inhibit CYP2C19 activation of clopidogrel — prefer pantoprazole.

interactions.title: Statin myopathy risk
interactions.note: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitor raises atorvastatin levels — cap atorvastatin at 20 mg or pause it during the course.

interactions.title: Colchicine toxicity
interactions.note: Strong CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitor with colchicine can be fatal — avoid the combination.

interactions.title: Myopathy
interactions.note: Colchicine with a statin: report muscle pain.

interactions.title: QT prolongation
interactions.note: Domperidone with CYP3A4 inhibitors or QT-prolonging antimicrobials is contraindicated (arrhythmia).

interactions.title: Additive QT prolongation
interactions.note: Two QT-prolonging drugs — check ECG/electrolytes in high-risk patients or choose an alternative.

interactions.title: Serotonin syndrome / seizures
interactions.note: Tramadol with serotonergic drugs: serotonin toxicity and lowered seizure threshold.

interactions.title: Respiratory depression
interactions.note: Opioid with a benzodiazepine, gabapentinoid or Z-drug: profound sedation and respiratory depression — avoid or use lowest doses.

interactions.title: Additive sedation
interactions.note: Two CNS depressants — falls and respiratory depression.

interactions.title: Dual RAAS blockade
interactions.note: ACE inhibitor with ARB: hyperkalaemia and AKI with no outcome benefit — avoid.

interactions.title: Hyperkalaemia
interactions.note: RAAS blocker with a potassium-raising drug — check potassium within a week.

interactions.title: AKI risk ("triple whammy" with a diuretic)
interactions.note: NSAIDs with ACE inhibitors/ARBs (especially plus a diuretic) can cause acute kidney injury — avoid or monitor creatinine.

interactions.title: Methotrexate toxicity
interactions.note: Antifolate synergy — fatal marrow suppression reported. Avoid.

interactions.title: Raised methotrexate levels
interactions.note: Reduces methotrexate clearance — monitor blood counts and renal function.

interactions.title: Hypoglycaemia
interactions.note: Raises sulfonylurea levels — warn about hypoglycaemia and check glucose.

interactions.title: Tendon rupture
interactions.note: Fluoroquinolone with a corticosteroid — higher tendon rupture risk, especially over 60.

interactions.title: GI bleeding
interactions.note: NSAID with a corticosteroid — add PPI cover.

interactions.title: Bleeding risk
interactions.note: SSRIs impair platelet function — GI bleeding with NSAIDs/antiplatelets/anticoagulants. Consider PPI cover.

interactions.title: Bradycardia / heart block
interactions.note: Beta-blocker with a rate-limiting calcium-channel blocker: risk of severe bradycardia and AV block.

interactions.title: Marrow suppression
interactions.note: Allopurinol blocks thiopurine metabolism — reduce the thiopurine to 25% or avoid.

interactions.title: Reduced absorption
interactions.note: Take levothyroxine on an empty stomach, 4 hours apart from calcium or iron.

interactions.title: Chelation
interactions.note: Calcium/iron reduce absorption — separate by at least 2 hours.

interactions.title: Theophylline toxicity
interactions.note: Ciprofloxacin raises theophylline levels.

interactions.title: Disulfiram-like reaction
interactions.note: Avoid alcohol during and for 48–72 h after.

interactions.title: Altered levels
interactions.note: Phenytoin interacts with azoles, valproate and anticoagulants — monitor levels/INR.

interactions.title: Altered levels
interactions.note: Monitor antiepileptic levels.

interactions.title: Severe hypotension
interactions.note: PDE-5 inhibitor with a nitrate — contraindicated.
